chunks: And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام that he said:
“Whoever performs the prostration of gratitude while in a state of wudu (ablution), Allah writes for him thereby ten blessings and erases from him ten grave sins.”

key_terms.سَجْدَةَ الشُّكْرِ: the prostration of gratitude offered in thanks to Allah
key_terms.صَلَوَاتٍ: blessings or merciful favors written by Allah for the servant
key_terms.مُتَوَضِّئٌ: being in a state of wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for performing Sajdat al-Shukr in a state of wudu?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the merit of Sajdat al-Shukr when performed in a state of wudu (ablution). It teaches that this act of grateful worship brings divine reward and the erasure of major sins.
